A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GEPO and HeteroRL. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3-1.7B reinforcement-learning results on MATH500 under different delays, training diagnostics and synthetic distribution experiments.

after.justification: v6 reports original Qwen3-1.7B/8B benchmark results, weighting ablations, think/non-think experiments and training diagnostics. Appendix A also adds a sampled-token analysis.

M1.justification: The core group-expectation weight and GEPO coefficient code remain unchanged. v6 removes v1 Section 3.3's explicit defensive-mixture component and recasts it as future work in Appendix H; Appendix D introduces local group reward aggregation without global gathering. v1 explicitly excluded defensive sampling from its reported comparisons, so its removal does not establish changed experimental GEPO updates.

E1.justification: v1 trains on MATH levels 3–5 and evaluates on MATH500. v6 retains this coverage and adds actual AMC2023, AIME2024 and AIME2025 evaluations in Tables 1–5, substantially broadening mathematical benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates GRPO and GSPO. v6 adds BNPO, explicitly identified as Beta Normalization Policy Optimization, and Dr.GRPO to online comparisons and the 1.7B supplementary online/heterogeneous comparisons (Tables 1, 3 and 5). GRPO and GSPO remain, including in the 8B heterogeneous comparison.

E3.justification: v6 adds 8B experiments and separate 2k/4k-output and think/non-think configurations beyond v1's 1.7B setup. Figure 1 also changes the displayed GRPO/GSPO advantage normalization to retain the standard-deviation divisor, although Listing 1's claim that only importance weights differ leaves implementation controls unclear. Pass@1 over eight responses, three epochs and the online/heterogeneous KL rules are retained. Newly disclosed token limits do not establish that v1's limits changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Bernoulli/Gaussian and latency/correlation analyses, v6 adds think/non-think performance and rollout-length/truncation analyses (Appendix B.5, Figure 9), a dedicated weighting ablation with additional variant results (Table 4), a 128-token distribution check (Appendix A), and a comparative response case study (Appendix G). These substantially expand diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v6 adds an A summary of 0.432 ± 0.36 from 128 generated tokens in Appendix A, although its dispersion terminology is unclear. v1's explicit shared-random-seed statement disappears. The correlation analyses retain their 95% confidence intervals and alpha = 0.05; neither version establishes repeated-training-seed uncertainty for the benchmark tables.

E6.justification: The result tables are substantially replaced and expanded. v1 Table 2 reports GEPO MATH500 best/last scores of 78.5/77.3 online and 75.3/74.4 at delay 64; v6 Table 3 reports 80.4/78.1 and 79.6/79.6 under its explicitly specified 1.7B, 2k setting. Numerous 8B, competition-benchmark, ablation and non-think results are added. Incompletely matched generation settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. The 0.76/0.96/0.78 correlations are retained.

T1.justification: The variance formulas, lemma, theorem and n-squared-plus-one bound in Appendix A are essentially retained. v6 adds the token-gradient matrix comparison in Section 3.2, Equation 5. Conversely, v1's explicit defensive-mixture Equation 15 and its epsilon-equals-one policy-gradient equivalence argument are removed.

C1.justification: The central HeteroRL/GEPO contributions and the 1800-second/3% performance-loss claim remain. v6's introduction explicitly extends the stated tolerance to 'arbitrary delays,' broadening the applicability language. Its new 85% best-to-last-gap statistic in the abstract quantifies the retained stability claim rather than introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: v6 adds substantive interpretations of reasoning-length, truncation, exploration and efficiency tradeoffs, including recommendations for non-think GEPO in latency-sensitive settings. It expands the shared-denominator gradient explanation and analyzes repetition and ineffective reflection in a response case study. Defensive sampling becomes a future hypothesis, conflicting with the retained author-contribution statement claiming experimental benefits. Earlier qualifications about estimator bias and high-latency performance dips remain.

D1.justification: v6 states that code is released and supplies a repository address. It newly documents 8,290 training samples, input/output limits, model provenance, the non-think prompt, A100/Ascend hardware labels and local reward aggregation. It drops v1's bfloat16, Flash Attention-2 and vLLM memory-cap 0.45 disclosures. Most simulated-delay and ZeroMQ details are retained in Appendix C rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v6 adds an IMPALA/V-trace comparison and references supporting the new baselines, datasets and reasoning-efficiency discussion. It removes the detailed Online DPO discussion and Calandriello citation; Noukhovitch remains cited in the introduction, while Section 5 now assigns the earlier theoretical-exploration claim to Wu. Positioning HeteroRL around unpredictable heterogeneous-network latency remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, results discussion, related work and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The method narrative foregrounds group-level weighting and gradient comparison, while implementation, network descriptions, token/sequence explanations and RL-paradigm comparisons move into thematic appendices. A contents page and reorganized appendix structure substantially change the reading order.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned into separate algorithm blocks and stacked training plots; the HeteroRL schematic and training plots are redrawn. v6 adds rollout-length and communication/local-reward diagrams, restructures performance tables across models and benchmarks, and moves v1's paradigm table to Table 7. Persistent laboratory headers, a narrower text block and colored case-study panels further change the layout.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical support by testing whether the findings extend beyond one model size and MATH500, and by examining reasoning-mode, truncation and response failures. More explicit generation settings and code-access information also improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting problems: Section 4.2 claims a 1.5-point margin where Table 1 gives 51.1 minus 49.9 = 1.2, and baseline controls and defensive-sampling status remain inconsistently described.
